title: Will you settle abroad?
What your chart looks at.
summary: The far rooms of your chart, the planet of all things foreign, and how an astrologer reads the pull of a life away from where you started.
film: Will you settle abroad? What your chart looks at
imageAlt: Maya with her suitcase beside a departures board that lists Rahu, room 9 and room 12
basis: This guide uses your rising sign and the planets in your birth chart, which depend on your exact time of birth.
inside: The three rooms of your chart that hold home and far away
The sign on each of them, by rising sign, in one table
Rahu, the planet of all things foreign, and what he wants
Whose far rooms the sky is visiting right now, with dates
intro: Some people know from childhood that they will end up somewhere else. Others never think about it until a job offer, a partner or a course of study pulls them across a border. Vedic astrology has a fairly clear idea of where that pull shows up in a chart, and it is not one placement but a small pattern.

This guide walks through that pattern the way an astrologer would: the rooms of the chart that hold home and far away, the planet tied to foreign things, and the slow planets in the sky that switch the theme on for a while. It cannot tell you where you will live. It shows you what is being looked at, so a reading makes sense when you get one.

sections.label: The rooms
title: Home, and the two
far rooms.
paragraphs: Your chart is divided into twelve houses, like a house with twelve rooms, each one in charge of a part of life. Three of them matter most for a life abroad. One holds where you come from, and two hold how far you go.

items.name: The 4th house: home
items.text: Your home, your mother, your roots and the land you grew up in. In this question it stands for the place you start from, and how strongly it holds on to you.

items.name: The 9th house: long journeys
items.text: Long journeys, higher learning, teachers and fortune. Study abroad and travel that changes how you see the world are read from here.

items.name: The 12th house: foreign lands
items.text: Foreign lands, far places and a life away from where you were born. It is also the house of spending, of rest and of letting go, which is why moving far is often read here with its costs.

sections.label: Look yourself up
title: Your far rooms,
by rising sign.
paragraphs: Which sign sits on each room depends on your rising sign, the sign that was coming up over the eastern horizon when you were born. With whole-sign houses, the sign right before your rising sign is your 12th house. Find your rising sign below: the first sign is your room of foreign lands, then your room of long journeys and your room of home.
after: Once you know the signs, look at which planets sit in them in your chart, and where the keepers of those signs sit. Busy far rooms and links between them and Rahu are what an astrologer is looking for.

sections.label: The planet
title: Rahu, the planet
of all things foreign.
paragraphs: Rahu is one of the two lunar nodes, drawn as a head with no body: a hunger that is never quite full. In the tradition he stands for what is foreign, unusual and outside the family pattern: other countries, other cultures, new technology and anything that breaks with where you started.

That is why he matters so much here. Rahu in the 12th or 9th house, Rahu joined to the keeper of one of those rooms, or Rahu running the current planetary period, are all read as a strong pull toward a life somewhere else. His hunger is the useful part: he is said to make people restless enough to go.

sections.label: The method
title: How an astrologer
reads it.
paragraphs: No single placement decides it. Astrologers look for several signs pointing the same way, and then for a time when they are switched on.

steps.name: Look at the far rooms
steps.text: Are there planets in the 12th and 9th houses? Which planets keep those rooms, and are they strong? Busy far rooms are read as a life with a lot of distance in it.

steps.name: Look at the home room
steps.text: A strong, settled 4th house is read as roots that pull you back. When the keeper of the 4th sits in the 12th, or the 4th is quiet while the far rooms are busy, the tradition reads it as a home that may be made somewhere else.

steps.name: Find Rahu
steps.text: Where Rahu sits and which rooms he touches is the next clue. Linked to the 12th or 9th, he is read as the foreign pull itself.

steps.name: Find the window
steps.text: The planetary periods, the dasha, set the timing. A period run by Rahu, or by the keeper of the 12th or 9th, is when the theme tends to come alive. The slow planets passing over the far rooms in the sky add weight to it.

sections.label: Right now
title: Whose far rooms
the sky is visiting.
paragraphs: These are read from your Moon sign, the sign the Moon was in when you were born, and they describe the sky for everyone with that Moon sign. They are seasons for the theme, not promises about a move.

rows.note: Until January 23 2027: the room of foreign lands is lit by the planet of growth.
Until January 23 2027: a season for long journeys, teachers and study.
Until December 4 2026, when Rahu moves on.
From December 5 2026 until June 2028: a big appetite for faraway places and new ideas.
From December 5 2026 until June 2028: the foreign pull is strong, and so is spending.
From January 24 to June 24 2027, while Jupiter is in Cancer.

after: Jupiter turns retrograde on December 12 2026 and stays in Leo until January 23, then moves into Cancer. Rahu moves from Aquarius into Capricorn on December 5 2026 and stays there for about a year and a half.

sections.label: The catch
title: Far isn’t lost.
Pack a bit of home.
paragraphs: The 12th house is the room of foreign lands, but it is also the room of spending and of missing what you left. The tradition is honest about that: a busy 12th is read as a life with real distance in it, and distance has a cost, in money and in feeling far from your people.

The usual advice is practical. Plan the costs of a move before you make it, keep up the ties you care about, and take something of home with you: a ritual, a recipe, a weekly call. A strong 4th house is not a reason to stay, and a busy 12th is not an order to leave. They tell you where the pull is, so you can choose with your eyes open.

faq.q: Does Rahu in the 12th house mean I will live abroad?
faq.a: Not on its own. It is read as a strong pull toward far places, but an astrologer looks for several signs pointing the same way, and for a period when they are switched on, before reading it as a life abroad.

faq.q: Should I use my Moon sign or my rising sign?
faq.a: For your own chart, the rising sign: it decides which sign sits on each room. The Moon sign is used for the slow planets in the sky right now, which is how the films and the table of who is being visited are read.

faq.q: I don’t know my rising sign. How do I find it?
faq.a: Your birth chart shows it, and it needs your time of birth. Draw yours on the home page and you can ask the astrologer what your far rooms hold. Your first question is free.

note: House meanings are those of the classical Parashari tradition, with whole-sign houses. Planet positions use the Lahiri ayanamsa; dates are US Eastern.
